topics.title: Meaning of Tax and Constitutional Framework
explain: Tax is a compulsory financial levy imposed by the government to fund public welfare expenses.
Article 366(28) defines taxation as including any tax or impost, whether general, local, or special.
Direct tax is levied directly on income/wealth and its burden cannot be shifted (e.g., Income-tax).
Indirect tax is levied on prices of goods/services and its burden is passed on to consumers (e.g., GST, Customs Duty).
Article 265 mandates that no tax can be levied or collected except by authority of law.
Article 246 and Seventh Schedule grant power to Parliament (Union List I), State Legislatures (State List II), or both (Concurrent List III).
Entry 82 of the Union List empowers Parliament to tax income other than agricultural income.

flow.title: Constitutional Source of Tax Power
steps: Article 265 requires legal authority
Article 246 activates 7th Schedule
Entry 82 List I grants Parliament power
Levy tax on non-agricultural income

topics.example: Paying income tax on your salary is a direct tax, whereas paying GST on a restaurant bill is an indirect tax passed to you.
remember: Entry 82 of Union List I empowers tax on income excluding agricultural income.
Article 265: No tax without authority of law.
mistakes: Confusing direct tax with indirect tax shifting: direct tax burden cannot be shifted to another person.

quiz.q: Which Entry of the Union List gives Parliament the power to levy tax on income other than agricultural income?
quiz.why: Entry 82 of List I in the Seventh Schedule to Article 246 empowers Parliament to tax non-agricultural income.

quiz.q: Under Article 265 of the Constitution of India:
o: Taxes can be levied by executive orders
No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law
State governments cannot levy any tax
Taxes can be collected without legislation during emergencies
quiz.why: Article 265 strictly states that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law.

topics.title: Components of Income-tax Law and Structure of an Act
explain: Income-tax law in India comprises the Income-tax Act, Annual Finance Acts, Income-tax Rules, Circulars/Notifications, and Court Decisions.
The Income-tax Act, 2025 governs the primary provisions, extending to all of India with 23 chapters, 536 sections, and 16 schedules.
Annual Finance Act introduces yearly amendments passed via the Finance Bill in Parliament's Budget Session.
Income-tax Rules, 2026 are framed by CBDT under section 2(80) powers ('as prescribed') for proper administration.
Circulars issued by CBDT clarify doubts and bind the Department, while Notifications issued by Central Govt/CBDT bind both Department and assessees.
Act structure follows a hierarchy: Section -> Sub-section (numbers) -> Clause (letters) -> Sub-clause (roman numerals).

flow.title: Hierarchy of Statutory Interpretation
steps: Income-tax Act 2025 lays basic law
Annual Finance Act amends rates yearly
Income-tax Rules 2026 provide procedures
CBDT Circulars & Notifications clarify details
Judicial decisions resolve disputes

topics.example: Section 19(2)(c)(i) breaks down as Section 19, Sub-section (2), Clause (c), and Sub-clause (i).
remember: Income-tax Act 2025 contains 23 Chapters, 536 Sections, and 16 Schedules.
Circulars bind the tax department, not the assessee.
mistakes: Assuming CBDT circulars are binding on assessees; assessees can take advantage of beneficial circulars but are not strictly bound by them.

quiz.q: Which component of income-tax law is issued by CBDT to clarify doubts and binds the tax department?
quiz.why: Circulars are issued by the CBDT for guidance and bind the department officers.

quiz.q: In legal citation section 19(1)(a), '(a)' represents the:
quiz.why: In section 19(1)(a), 19 is section, (1) is sub-section, and (a) is clause.

topics.title: Charge of Income Tax
explain: Section 4 is the charging section and backbone of the Income-tax Act, creating the legal liability to pay tax.
Tax is charged at rates specified by the Annual Finance Act, the Income-tax Act, 2025 (e.g. section 202), or both.
Income-tax includes additional income-tax or surcharge levied under the Act.
The charge is levied on every 'person' defined under section 2(77).
Tax is charged on total income earned during the tax year, unless covered by specific exceptions allowing same-year assessment.

flow.title: Mechanism of Section 4 Charge
steps: Identify Person u/s 2(77)
Determine Total Income for Tax Year
Apply Slab or Special Tax Rates
Compute Tax Liability

topics.example: Even if you earn income across 12 months, Section 4 creates the legal charge to assess that income under the relevant tax regime.
remember: Section 4 is the charging section of the Income-tax Act, 2025.
Tax liability of any entity springs directly from Section 4.
mistakes: Thinking income tax can be levied without a specific charging section; Section 4 is essential to create tax liability.

quiz.q: Which section acts as the charging section under the Income-tax Act, 2025?
quiz.why: Section 4 is the charging section providing the legal authority to levy income tax.

quiz.q: Under Section 4, tax is charged on the total income earned during:
quiz.why: Section 4 charges tax on the total income earned during the tax year.

topics.title: Assessee and Assessment Definitions
explain: Assessee u/s 2(11) means any person by whom tax or any other sum of money (interest/penalty) is payable under the Act.
Includes every person against whom proceedings have been initiated for assessment of income, loss, or refund (for self or others).
Includes deemed assessees (e.g., legal representative of a deceased person) and assessees-in-default (e.g., employer failing to deposit TDS).
Rule: Every assessee is a person, but every person need not be an assessee.
Assessment u/s 2(13) is the procedure by which the Assessing Officer determines an assessee's income; includes reassessment and recomputation.

flow.title: Scope of Assessee
steps: Person owing tax or sum
Person facing tax proceedings
Deemed Assessee by law
Assessee-in-Default for non-compliance

topics.example: If an employer deducts tax from employee salary but fails to deposit it with the government, the employer becomes an 'assessee-in-default'.
remember: Assessee: Section 2(11); Assessment: Section 2(13).
Every assessee is a person, but not every person is an assessee.
mistakes: Believing a person with income below exemption limit facing no proceedings or dues is an assessee.

quiz.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding an assessee?
o: Every person is automatically an assessee
Every assessee is a person, but every person need not be an assessee
A person filing return with zero income and no dues is always an assessee-in-default
quiz.why: A person becomes an assessee only if tax/sum is payable or proceedings/defaults apply.

quiz.q: Assessment under Section 2(13) includes:
quiz.why: Section 2(13) defines assessment to include reassessment and recomputation.

topics.title: Concept of Person - Individual, HUF, Firm, and AOP/BOI
explain: Section 2(77) defines 'person' under seven distinct tax categories.
Individual: Natural human beings, including minors, lunatics (assessed via guardians), and deceased persons (via legal reps).
HUF: Separate entity consisting of male lineally descended members, wives, and daughters. Coparceners (up to 4th degree including Karta) acquire interest by birth and can demand partition.
Status of Daughter in HUF: Equal coparcenary rights w.e.f. 6th Sept 2005. Wives/daughters-in-law are members, not coparceners.
Schools of Hindu Law: Dayabhaga (WB & Assam - no right by birth while father lives); Mitakshara (Rest of India - right acquired by birth).
Firm u/s 2(45) & Partner u/s 2(74): Includes Partnership under 1932 Act and LLP under 2008 Act. Minor admitted to benefits is treated as partner.
AOP vs BOI: AOP members (individuals or non-individuals) combine voluntarily for a common purpose to produce income; BOI consists ONLY of individuals.

flow.title: Distinguishing Entities in Person Definition
steps: Individual: Natural human being
HUF: Joint family with coparcenary rights
Firm/LLP: Business association of partners
AOP: Any persons joining for income
BOI: Only individuals joining together

topics.example: A company, a firm, and an individual joining together to build a bridge form an AOP, but cannot form a BOI because BOI allows only natural individuals.
remember: Daughters acquired equal coparcenary rights in HUF from 6th September, 2005.
BOI consists of ONLY individuals; AOP can include companies/firms.
mistakes: Confusing Dayabhaga and Mitakshara: Dayabhaga applies in West Bengal & Assam where children get no right by birth while father lives.

quiz.q: Under the Mitakshara School of Hindu Law, a person acquires right in the family property by:
quiz.why: In Mitakshara school (rest of India), coparcenary right is acquired by birth.

quiz.q: What is the key distinction between an Association of Persons (AOP) and a Body of Individuals (BOI)?
o: BOI can have corporate members while AOP cannot
BOI members can only be natural individuals, whereas AOP members can be any entity
AOP is not a person under Section 2(77)
quiz.why: BOI is strictly comprised of individuals, whereas AOP members can include companies or firms.

topics.title: Concept of Person - Companies, Local Authority & Artificial Juridical Person
explain: Company u/s 2(28): Indian company, foreign body corporate, entity assessed as company under 1961 Act, or entity declared by CBDT.
Domestic Company u/s 2(42): Indian company OR foreign company making prescribed arrangements in India for dividend declaration/payment out of Indian taxable income.
Indian Company u/s 2(53): Formed & registered under Indian company law with registered/principal office in India.
Foreign Company u/s 2(46): A company that is NOT a domestic company.
Public Interest Classification: Widely Held (substantial public interest u/s 2(29) e.g., Govt/RBI 40%+ owned, Sec 8 co, Nidhi, listed public co) vs Closely Held (private companies).
Local Authority: Municipalities, District Boards, Port Commissioners managing local funds (exempt on local utility services like water/electricity).
Artificial Juridical Person: Residual legal entities like Deities/Idols, Bar Councils, and Public Universities.

flow.title: Classification of Companies
steps: Check incorporation & registered office
If Indian/Indian dividend setup -> Domestic Co
If not Domestic Co -> Foreign Co
Check Public Interest -> Widely Held vs Closely Held

topics.example: A deity of a public temple or a state university is assessed as an Artificial Juridical Person.
remember: Indian Company requires both registration in India AND principal/registered office in India.
All private limited companies are treated as closely held companies.
mistakes: Treating all foreign-incorporated companies automatically as foreign companies without checking if domestic dividend arrangements were made.

quiz.q: A foreign company that makes prescribed arrangements in India for declaration and payment of dividends out of its Indian income is classified as a:
quiz.why: Section 2(42) defines domestic company to include foreign companies making prescribed Indian dividend arrangements.

quiz.q: A public university or a deity of a temple falls under which category of 'Person' u/s 2(77)?
quiz.why: Entities with legal personality not falling under other categories are Artificial Juridical Persons.

topics.title: Tax Year and Exceptions to Same-Year Assessment
explain: Tax Year u/s 3: 12-month period of the financial year starting 1st April and ending 31st March.
Newly Set Up Business/Profession: Tax year starts from the date of setting up or new income source coming into existence and ends on 31st March.
General Rule: Income of a tax year is assessed to tax after the end of that tax year.
Exception 1 - Shipping Business of Non-Resident (Sec 316): 7.5% of carriage fare/freight is deemed income and taxed before ship leaves port.
Exception 2 - Persons Leaving India (Sec 317): Total income from 1st April to probable departure date taxed in current year if no intent to return.
Exception 3 - AOP/BOI/AJP for short event (Sec 318): Income taxed in same year if entity likely to dissolve in same or next year.
Exception 4 - Transfer of Property to Avoid Tax (Sec 319): Income taxed immediately upon proceedings if asset disposal is likely.
Exception 5 - Discontinued Business (Sec 320): Income from 1st April to discontinuance date may be taxed in same year at AO's discretion.

flow.title: Exceptions to Tax Year Rule (Accelerated Assessment)
steps: General Rule: Income assessed after Tax Year ends
Check accelerated assessment exceptions (Sec 316 to 320)
If exception applies, calculate income to departure/dissolution date
Charge tax in the same tax year

topics.example: If a non-resident shipping line loads cargo at Mumbai port, 7.5% of freight payable is taxed u/s 316 before the ship leaves.
remember: Non-resident shipping business u/s 316: 7.5% of freight/carriage is deemed income.
Discontinued business (Sec 320) assessment in same year is at the discretion of the AO.
mistakes: Assuming discontinued business MUST be assessed in the same year; Sec 320 gives discretion to the Assessing Officer.

quiz.q: If a professional sets up practice on 1st July 2026, the period of tax year for the first year will be:
quiz.why: For a newly set up profession, the tax year starts on the setup date (1.7.2026) and ends on 31st March.

quiz.q: Under Section 316, what percentage of freight paid/payable to a non-resident shipping business is deemed as income?
quiz.why: Section 316 deems 7.5% of the amount paid/payable for carriage of goods/passengers as taxable income.

topics.title: Definition and Concepts of Income
explain: Section 2(49) gives an inclusive definition of income ('Income includes...'), extending beyond standard accounting receipts.
Includes profits/gains, dividends, perquisites/salaries, business receipts, capital gains, lotteries/winnings, inventory conversion FMV, gifts/uncompensated property.
Regular vs Casual Receipts: Casual receipts like lottery winnings are expressly taxed as income.
Revenue vs Capital Receipts: Capital receipts are non-taxable UNLESS specifically included (e.g. Capital Gains u/s 67, termination compensation).
Net vs Gross: Income generally means net receipts after allowable head-wise expenditures.
Application of Income vs Diversion of Income: Application (discharging obligation after receipt) is TAXABLE; Diversion by overriding title (income diverted before reaching assessee) is NOT taxable.

flow.title: Income Classification & Taxability Test
steps: Receipt of money/benefit
Check if revenue nature or capital receipt
If capital, check specific inclusion u/s 2(49)
Test Diversion vs Application of Income
Compute net income under relevant head

topics.example: If a father directs salary to pay his loan after receiving it, it is Application of Income (taxable). If court orders 30% salary paid directly to ex-spouse before reaching him, it is Diversion by overriding title (not taxable to him).
remember: Section 2(49) definition of income is inclusive, not exhaustive.
Diversion of income by overriding title is not taxable in the hands of the assessee.
mistakes: Confusing application of income with diversion of income: voluntarily spending income after receiving it does not reduce taxable income.

quiz.q: Which of the following describes 'Diversion of Income' by overriding title?
o: Spending income on personal expenses after receipt
Transferring income before it reaches the assessee due to an legal obligation
Investing income in tax-saving fixed deposits
Gifting money to spouse out of net salary
quiz.why: Diversion of income occurs when income is diverted before reaching the assessee by an overriding legal obligation.

quiz.q: The statutory definition of 'Income' under Section 2(49) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 is:
quiz.why: The definition begins with 'Income includes', making it an inclusive definition.

topics.title: Unexplained Sources of Income and Tax Rate
explain: Section 102 - Unexplained Credits: Sums credited in books without satisfactory explanation from assessee/lender.
Section 103 - Unexplained Investments: Unrecorded investments or excess investment amounts not satisfactorily explained.
Section 104 - Unexplained Assets: Money, bullion, jewelry, virtual digital assets, etc. owned but unrecorded or under-recorded.
Section 105 - Unexplained Expenditure: Incurred expenses with no satisfactory source explanation (no deduction allowed against this income).
Section 106 - Hundi Borrowing/Repayment: Amounts borrowed or repaid on hundi/negotiable instruments otherwise than by account-payee cheque.
Taxation u/s 195: Taxed at a flat rate of 30% + 25% surcharge + 4% cess = Effective rate of 39%. No basic exemption or deduction/loss set-off allowed.

flow.title: Processing Unexplained Income
steps: Discovery of unrecorded cash/credit/asset
AO requests source explanation
If no or unsatisfactory explanation -> Deemed Income u/s 102-106
Apply Sec 195: 30% tax + 25% surcharge + 4% cess (39% effective)
Disallow any expense deduction or loss set-off

topics.example: If 300g gold worth ₹42.5 lakhs is found but books record only ₹21.5 lakhs with no valid explanation for the ₹21 lakh gap, ₹21 lakhs is taxed u/s 104 @ 39%.
remember: Unexplained income sections: 102 to 106.
Effective tax rate u/s 195 = 30% + 25% surcharge + 4% cess = 39%.
mistakes: Claiming basic exemption limit or loss set-off against unexplained incomes; Section 195 strictly prohibits deductions and set-offs.

quiz.q: What is the effective tax rate (including surcharge and cess) applicable to unexplained incomes u/s 102 to 106 under Section 195?
quiz.why: 30% tax + 25% surcharge (7.5%) = 37.5% + 4% HEC (1.5%) = 39% effective rate.

quiz.q: Amount borrowed or repaid on a Hundi otherwise than through an account payee cheque is deemed as income under Section:
quiz.why: Section 106 deals with amounts borrowed or repaid on hundi/negotiable instruments.

topics.title: Definition of India and Agricultural Income Scope
explain: India u/s 2(52): Territory under Art 1, territorial waters, seabed/subsoil, continental shelf, EEZ, and airspace above territory/territorial waters.
Agricultural Income u/s 2(5): Includes rent/revenue from land, income from agricultural operations, processing to render produce fit for market, sale of produce, and farm building income.
Condition for Agri Rent: Land MUST be situated in India AND used for agricultural purposes (foreign agricultural land income is FULLY TAXABLE).
Ownership Rule: Ownership of land is NOT necessary to claim agricultural income (e.g., sub-tenant receiving agri rent qualifies).

Basic vs Subsequent Operations: Basic operations (tilling, sowing) require human skill/labour on land. Subsequent operations (weeding, digging) qualify ONLY if done in continuation of basic operations.

flow.title: Testing Agricultural Operations
steps: Land situated in India
Perform Basic Operations (tilling, sowing)
Perform Subsequent Operations in continuation
Resulting income -> Agricultural Income u/s 2(5)

topics.example: Rent received by a sub-tenant from a farmer for agricultural cultivation in Jaipur is exempt agricultural income even though the sub-tenant does not own the land.
remember: Agricultural land in a foreign country is fully taxable (not exempt).
Subsequent operations without basic operations do not constitute agriculture.
mistakes: Treating income from foreign agricultural land as exempt agricultural income under Section 2(5).

quiz.q: Income derived from agricultural land situated in Sri Lanka is:
quiz.why: Agricultural income must be derived from land situated in India to be exempt u/s 2(5).

quiz.q: Which of the following operations independently (without basic tilling/sowing) qualifies as an agricultural operation?
quiz.why: Subsequent operations qualify as agricultural operations only when performed in continuation of basic operations.

topics.title: Urban vs Rural Agricultural Land and Farm Buildings
explain: Farm Building Income: Qualifying as agricultural income requires building to be on/in immediate vicinity of land, required as dwelling/storehouse, and land assessed to land revenue/local rate.
Urban Agricultural Land u/s 2(22)(iii): Land situated inside Municipality/Cantonment board with population >= 10,000.
Aerial Distance Limits for Urban Land: (1) Within 2 km if population > 10,000 to 1,00,000; (2) Within 6 km if population > 1,00,000 to 10,00,000; (3) Within 8 km if population > 10,00,000.
Farm Building on Urban Land: Income from a farm building on urban agricultural land is NOT agricultural income (it is TAXABLE).
Transfer of Urban Agri Land: Capital gains from sale of urban agricultural land are taxable u/s 67, not exempt under Section 2(5).
Indirect Connection Exclusions: Income from livestock breeding, poultry, dairy farming, fisheries, managing agent commission, or spontaneous forest trees is NON-AGRICULTURAL.

flow.title: Determining Urban Land Status
steps: Check location relative to Municipality limit
Check population of local municipality
Apply aerial distance rule (2km / 6km / 8km)
If inside limit -> Urban Land (Farm bldg income taxable)
If outside limit -> Rural Land (Farm bldg income exempt)

topics.example: If land is 5 km aerially from a municipality of 3.5 lakh population, the 6 km rule applies, making it Urban Land; farm building income there is taxable.
remember: Aerial distance slabs: 2 km (>10k-1L), 6 km (>1L-10L), 8 km (>10L).
Dairy farming, poultry, and fisheries are NON-AGRICULTURAL income.
mistakes: Assuming income from dairy farming or sale of spontaneous forest trees is agricultural income due to land connection.

quiz.q: Agricultural land situated 5 km aerially from a municipality having a population of 8,00,000 is classified as:
quiz.why: For population between 1,00,000 and 10,00,000, land within 6 km aerial distance is urban agricultural land.

quiz.q: Which of the following receipts is classified as Agricultural Income?
o: Income from growing flowers and creepers
quiz.why: Growing flowers and creepers involves basic agricultural operations, unlike poultry, dairy, or livestock breeding.

topics.title: Apportionment of Composite Income & Special Business Rules
explain: Composite Income: Earned when an assessee grows agricultural produce and uses it as raw material in manufacturing business.
Rule 270 - General Apportionment: Deduct Market Value (MV) of agricultural produce from business sales proceeds to calculate business income. Agri Income = MV minus Cost of Cultivation.
Market Value Determination: Average market price during the tax year if raw produce is ordinarily sold; or (Expenses + Land Revenue + AO Reasonable Profit) if not ordinarily sold.
Rule 271 - Rubber Manufacture: 65% Agricultural Income, 35% Business Income.
Rule 271 - Coffee Grown & Cured: 75% Agricultural Income, 25% Business Income.
Rule 271 - Coffee Grown, Cured, Roasted & Grounded: 60% Agricultural Income, 40% Business Income.
Rule 271 - Tea Grown & Manufactured: 60% Agricultural Income, 40% Business Income.

flow.title: Rule 271 Composite Income Split
steps: Compute total composite business profit
Identify commodity (Rubber / Coffee / Tea)
Apply Rule 271 percentage split
Separate Exempt Agri Income from Taxable Business Income

topics.example: If Mr. C earns ₹12 lakhs profit growing rubber plants and manufacturing latex in India, Agri Income = 65% of ₹12L (₹7.8L) and Business Income = 35% (₹4.2L).
remember: Rubber: 65% Agri / 35% Business.
Coffee (grown & cured): 75% Agri / 25% Business.
Coffee (roasted & grounded): 60% Agri / 40% Business.
Tea: 60% Agri / 40% Business.
mistakes: Applying Rule 271 percentages to gross turnover instead of total net computed profits.

quiz.q: Under Rule 271, what proportion of income from sale of tea grown and manufactured by the seller in India is treated as business income?
quiz.why: For tea manufacture, 60% is agricultural income and 40% is taxable business income.

quiz.q: If an assessee earns ₹10,00,000 total profit from growing and curing coffee in India, the taxable business income is:
quiz.why: For coffee grown and cured, 25% is business income (25% of ₹10,00,000 = ₹2,50,000).

topics.title: Steps for Computation of Total Income & Tax Liability
explain: Step 1: Determine residential status.
Step 2: Classify income into 5 heads u/s 13 (Salaries, House Property, PGBP, Capital Gains, Other Sources).
Step 3: Compute income under each head (applying Section 14 disallowance for expenses related to exempt income).
Step 4: Apply clubbing provisions for income of spouse, minor child, etc.
Step 5: Apply set-off and carry forward of losses.
Step 6 & 7: Arrive at Gross Total Income (GTI) and subtract Chapter VIII deductions.
Step 8 to 15: Arrive at Total Income (round off u/s 516 to nearest ₹10), apply tax rates/surcharge/cess, deduct advance tax/TDS, and determine final Tax Payable/Refundable.

flow.title: Complete 15-Step Income Tax Computation
steps: Determine Residential Status & Heads of Income
Compute Net Head-wise Incomes (Sec 14 disallowance)
Clubbing & Set-off of Losses -> GTI
Deduct Chapter VIII Allowances -> Total Income
Apply Tax Rates, Rebate u/s 156, Surcharge & 4% Cess
Adjust TDS/TCS & Advance Tax -> Net Payable u/s 516

topics.example: Expenditure incurred to earn exempt dividend or agricultural income is disallowed u/s 14 and cannot reduce taxable salary or business income.
remember: Section 14: No deduction allowed for expenses incurred in earning exempt income.
Total income and final tax payable must be rounded off to the nearest multiple of ₹10 u/s 516.
mistakes: Deducting expenses incurred for earning exempt agricultural income against taxable business income.

quiz.q: Under Section 14 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, expenditure incurred in relation to income which does not form part of total income is:
o: Not allowed as deduction under any head
Allowed only under the default tax regime
quiz.why: Section 14 disallows any expenditure incurred in relation to exempt income.

quiz.q: Total income computed under the Income-tax Act is rounded off to the nearest multiple of ₹10 under Section:
quiz.why: Section 516 provides for rounding off total income and net tax payable to the nearest multiple of ₹10.

topics.title: Default Tax Regime u/s 202 vs Optional Tax Regime
explain: Default Tax Regime (Sec 202): Applies automatically unless individual/HUF/AOP/BOI/AJP opts out u/s 202(4). Basic exemption limit is ₹4,00,000.

Disallowed Benefits u/s 202(2): Standard exemptions (HRA, LTC, MP/MLA allowances, minor child income exemption) and Chapter VIII deductions (except Sec 124 NPS, Sec 125 Agnipath, Sec 146 new employees).
Loss Restrictions u/s 202(2): No set-off of house property loss against any other head.

Opt-out Rules u/s 202(4): Non-business individuals can opt out every year in ITR u/s 263(1). Business individuals can opt out once, but if they opt back in, they can NEVER opt out again while holding business income.
Optional Tax Regime (Old): Basic exemption ₹2,50,000 (Senior Citizen ₹3,00,000; Very Senior Citizen ₹5,00,000). Slabs: 2.5L-5L (5%), 5L-10L (20%), >10L (30%).

flow.title: Regime Selection & Opt-Out Rules
steps: Default Regime u/s 202 applies (₹4L exemption)
Check if assessee has Business/Profession income
If No Business: Choose default or optional regime yearly in ITR
If Business: Opt-out once; if withdrawn, forever locked in Default Regime

topics.example: An individual with ₹16,00,000 income under Section 202 pay tax: Nil (first 4L) + ₹20k (5% of 4L) + ₹40k (10% of 4L) + ₹60k (15% of 4L) = ₹1,20,000 + 4% HEC.
remember: Basic exemption limit under Default Tax Regime u/s 202 is ₹4,00,000.
Senior citizen higher basic exemption (₹3L / ₹5L) is available ONLY under the Optional Tax Regime.
mistakes: Assuming senior citizens get a ₹5,00,000 basic exemption limit under the Default Tax Regime u/s 202.

quiz.q: What is the basic exemption limit for an individual paying tax under the Default Tax Regime under Section 202(1)?
quiz.why: The basic exemption limit under section 202(1) default tax regime is ₹4,00,000.

quiz.q: Under Section 202(4), an individual having income from business or profession who opts out of the default tax regime and later withdraws the option can:
o: Never opt out of the default tax regime again while having business income
Opt out only with CBDT approval
quiz.why: Section 202(4) specifies that business assessees who withdraw their opt-out can never opt out again as long as they have business income.

topics.title: Special Tax Rates for Specific Incomes
explain: Special tax rates apply to specific income categories regardless of whether the assessee pays tax under the default or optional tax regime.
Section 197: Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on capital assets taxed @ 12.5%.
Section 198: LTCG on STT-paid equity shares / equity-oriented funds / business trust units taxed @ 12.5% on amount exceeding ₹1.25 lakhs.
Section 196: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) on STT-paid equity shares / equity-oriented funds / business trust units taxed @ 20%.
Section 194 (Table SI No. 1 & 5): Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, races, card games, gambling, or online games taxed @ 30%.
Section 194 (Table SI No. 4): Income from transfer of Virtual Digital Assets (VDA) taxed @ 30%.

flow.title: Taxing Special Incomes
steps: Separate Special Rate Incomes from Total Income
Apply Sec 194 for Winnings/VDA (30%)
Tax remaining balance income at normal slab rates

topics.example: If total income includes ₹2,00,000 LTCG u/s 198, ₹1.25 lakhs is exempt and remaining ₹75,000 is taxed at a special rate of 12.5%.
remember: Sec 198 LTCG exemption threshold = ₹1.25 lakhs (taxed @ 12.5% above it).
Sec 196 STCG special rate = 20%.
mistakes: Applying slab rates or basic exemption adjustments directly to lottery winnings or VDA gains; special flat rates apply.

quiz.q: Under Section 198, Long-Term Capital Gains on STT-paid equity shares are taxable at what rate on amounts exceeding ₹1.25 lakhs?
quiz.why: Section 198 taxes eligible LTCG in excess of ₹1.25 lakhs at 12.5%.

quiz.q: What is the special rate of tax applicable to Short-Term Capital Gains u/s 196 on STT-paid equity shares?
quiz.why: Section 196 specifies a 20% tax rate on STT-paid short-term capital gains.

topics.title: Tax Rates for Non-Individual Entities (Firms, Companies, Co-operatives)
explain: Firm / LLP / Local Authority: Taxed at a flat rate of 30% on total income.
Co-operative Society Normal Slabs: Up to ₹10,000 (10%), ₹10,001-₹20,000 (20%), Above ₹20,000 (30%). Option u/s 203 allows concessional 22% flat rate.
Domestic Company Normal Rates: (1) 25% if turnover in FY 2024-25 <= ₹400 crore; (2) 22% if exercising option u/s 200; (3) 30% in any other case.
Foreign Company Tax Rates: Royalties/FTS under pre-1976 approved agreements taxed @ 50%; all other income taxed @ 35%.

flow.title: Corporate & Entity Tax Rate Path
steps: Check Entity Type
Firm / LLP -> Flat 30%
Domestic Co -> Check Turnover (<=400Cr? 25%) or Sec 200 (22%) or Other (30%)
Foreign Co -> Royalty/FTS (50%) or Other (35%)

topics.example: A domestic company with FY 2024-25 turnover of ₹350 crore pays tax at 25% under normal provisions.
remember: Domestic company turnover threshold for 25% rate = ₹400 crore in FY 2024-25.
Foreign company general tax rate = 35%.
mistakes: Applying 25% rate to a domestic company whose turnover exceeded ₹400 crore in FY 2024-25.

quiz.q: A domestic company having a total turnover of ₹350 crore in the tax year 2024-25 will be subject to income tax at the rate of:
quiz.why: Domestic companies with turnover <= ₹400 crore in FY 2024-25 are taxed at 25%.

quiz.q: The general rate of income-tax applicable to a Foreign Company on its general income is:
quiz.why: Foreign companies are taxed at 35% on general income under current provisions.

topics.title: Surcharge & Marginal Relief Mechanics
explain: Surcharge on Individuals/HUF/AOP/BOI/AJP under Default Regime (Sec 202): (1) Total income > ₹50L to ≤ ₹1Cr = 10%; (2) > ₹1Cr to ≤ ₹2Cr = 15%; (3) > ₹2Cr = 25% (capped at 15% on dividend & capital gains u/s 196, 197, 198). Maximum surcharge is 25%.
Surcharge under Optional Regime: Surcharge slabs are 10% (>50L), 15% (>1Cr), 25% (>2Cr), and 37% (>5Cr; capped at 15% for dividend/capital gains).
Surcharge on Firms/LLP: 12% if total income exceeds ₹1 crore.
Surcharge on Domestic Companies: 7% if income > ₹1 crore to ≤ ₹10 crore; 12% if income > ₹10 crore. (10% flat if opted for Sec 200).
Surcharge on Foreign Companies: 2% if income > ₹1 crore to ≤ ₹10 crore; 5% if income > ₹10 crore.

Marginal Relief: Ensures tax increase (including surcharge) does not exceed the income increase beyond the threshold. Formula: Wn = Un + Vn, where Un is tax on threshold limit and Vn is income exceeding threshold.

flow.title: Marginal Relief Computation
steps: Calculate Tax + Surcharge on Total Income (Amount A)
Calculate Tax on threshold income (e.g. ₹50L / ₹1Cr) = Un
Calculate Excess Income over threshold = Vn
Compute Cap Wn = Un + Vn
Tax payable = Lower of A or Wn; Relief = A - Wn

topics.example: If total income is ₹51,00,000 under Default Regime, tax + surcharge is capped so that extra tax payable doesn't exceed the ₹1,00,000 excess income over ₹50 lakhs.
remember: Maximum surcharge under Default Tax Regime u/s 202 is capped at 25%.
Surcharge on dividend and capital gains u/s 196, 197, 198 cannot exceed 15%.
mistakes: Applying 37% surcharge under Default Tax Regime u/s 202; 37% surcharge exists ONLY under the Optional Tax Regime.

quiz.q: What is the maximum rate of surcharge applicable to an individual under the Default Tax Regime under Section 202?
quiz.why: Under default tax regime u/s 202, surcharge is capped at a maximum of 25%.

quiz.q: What rate of surcharge applies to a domestic company (not opting u/s 200) with a total income of ₹12 crore?
quiz.why: Domestic companies with total income exceeding ₹10 crore pay 12% surcharge.

topics.title: Tax Rebate for Resident Individuals
explain: Rebate u/s 156 provides tax relief strictly to RESIDENT INDIVIDUALS.
Rebate under Default Tax Regime u/s 202(1): Total income <= ₹12,00,000 -> 100% of tax or ₹60,000, whichever is lower (Tax liability = NIL).
Marginal Rebate u/s 156 (Default Regime): If total income exceeds ₹12,00,000 marginally and tax payable exceeds the excess income over ₹12L, rebate = Tax payable minus excess income over ₹12L.
Rebate under Optional Tax Regime: Total income <= ₹5,00,000 -> 100% of tax or ₹12,500, whichever is lower.
Exclusions: Rebate under Optional Regime is NOT available against tax payable on LTCG u/s 198. Under Default Regime, rebate cannot exceed tax computed u/s 202(1).
Rebate is applied BEFORE adding 4% Health & Education Cess.

flow.title: Section 156 Rebate Steps (Default Regime)
steps: Verify: Assessee is Resident Individual
Check Total Income vs ₹12,00,000 limit
If <= ₹12L: Grant rebate up to ₹60,000 (Tax = Nil)
If > ₹12L: Check Marginal Rebate (Tax vs Excess over 12L)
Apply rebate BEFORE adding 4% HEC

topics.example: A resident individual with ₹10,50,000 income under default regime has ₹45,00,000 computed tax. Rebate u/s 156 is ₹45,000, making tax liability NIL.
remember: Max rebate under Default Regime = ₹60,00,000 (Income limit ₹12L).
Max rebate under Optional Regime = ₹12,500 (Income limit ₹5L).
Rebate u/s 156 is available ONLY to Resident Individuals.
mistakes: Granting Section 156 rebate to non-resident individuals, HUFs, or firms.

quiz.q: What is the maximum rebate available under Section 156 to a resident individual under the Default Tax Regime if total income is ₹11,50,000?
quiz.why: Under the default tax regime, Section 156 allows 100% tax rebate up to ₹60,00,000 for total income up to ₹12,00,000.

quiz.q: Section 156 tax rebate is available to which of the following assessees?
quiz.why: Rebate u/s 156 is strictly restricted to resident individuals.

topics.title: Partial Integration of Agricultural Income
explain: Partial Integration indirect mechanism: Aggregates net agricultural income with non-agricultural income to tax non-agricultural income at higher slab rates.
Applicability: Applies ONLY to Individuals, HUF, AOP, BOI, and Artificial Juridical Persons (Does NOT apply to companies, firms, LLPs, or co-operatives).

Conditions for Partial Integration: (1) Net agricultural income exceeds ₹5,000 p.a.; AND (2) Non-agricultural total income exceeds the basic exemption limit (₹4L under Default Regime; ₹2.5L / ₹3L / ₹5L under Optional Regime).
Calculation Formula: Zn = Xn - Yn.
Xn = Tax on Aggregate Income (Total Income + Net Agri Income).
Yn = Tax on (Net Agri Income + Basic Exemption Limit).
Net Tax Chargeable = Zn + Surcharge (if any) - Rebate u/s 156 + 4% HEC.

flow.title: Partial Integration Calculation (Zn = Xn - Yn)
steps: Check conditions: Net Agri > ₹5,000 & Non-Agri > Basic Exemption
Compute Aggregate Income = Total Income + Net Agri Income
Xn = Calculate Tax on Aggregate Income
Yn = Calculate Tax on (Net Agri Income + Basic Exemption)
Zn = Xn - Yn; Add Surcharge/HEC, subtract Rebate

topics.example: An individual aged 45 with non-agri income ₹18,30,000 and net agri income ₹3,10,000 satisfies both tests; tax is calculated on ₹21,40,000 (Xn) minus tax on ₹7,10,000 (Yn).
remember: Agri income threshold for partial integration = ₹5,000 p.a.
Partial integration does NOT apply to companies, firms, or LLPs.
mistakes: Applying partial integration to a company or firm earning agricultural income.

quiz.q: Partial integration of agricultural income with non-agricultural income applies only if net agricultural income exceeds:
quiz.why: Partial integration requires net agricultural income to exceed ₹5,000 per annum.

quiz.q: Which entity is subject to partial integration of agricultural income?
quiz.why: Partial integration applies to Individuals, HUFs, AOPs, BOIs, and AJPs, but not to companies, firms, or co-operatives.
